profile.campus: Time Warner Cable / Charter National Data Center West, Centennial CO (2 buildings, campus-level figures)
profile.address: 11011, East Peakview Avenue, Centennial, Arapahoe County, Colorado, 80111
profile.reading: This registry row is the second of two buildings mapped under the name Time Warner Datacenter in Centennial, Colorado, roughly 110 meters from its sibling row in this registry, together forming what Time Warner Cable, now Charter Communications under the Spectrum brand, calls its National Data Center West campus. Trade press coverage from Data Center Dynamics, drawing on a Time Warner Cable announcement, documents an $85 million expansion of this campus that broke ground in June 2013, completed construction in late 2014, and came online in January 2015, bringing the site to a total of 170,000 square feet, 1,600 equipment racks, and 6.4 megawatts of critical IT load, a 75 percent capacity increase over the pre-expansion facility, as part of a $141 million total investment including earlier 2011 upgrades. The press coverage states the campus delivers digital video and IP based services for Time Warner Cable's core residential and business products, supporting roughly 70 million daily residential emails and billing for more than 15 million customers at the time, alongside WiFi, high speed data, voice, TV, and the company's IntelligentHome offering, and that the company pursued LEED Silver certification for the facility. A separate data center industry public records aggregator, datacenter.fyi, lists the campus address at 7.649 megawatts of total power capacity with 4.59 megawatts of IT load and a power usage effectiveness rating of approximately 1.67, connected to the Public Service Company of Colorado grid, a more granular current capacity figure than the original expansion announcement's 6.4 MW critical load figure. Charter Communications absorbed Time Warner Cable in a 2016 merger and operates the combined company's residential cable, internet, and phone services under the Spectrum consumer brand. Charter and Spectrum branded data centers supporting these operations, including this campus, are not typically marketed as public colocation facilities, unlike wholesale or retail colocation operators tracked elsewhere in this registry. These campus level figures apply to the two building National Data Center West campus as a whole rather than to this specific building alone, since no source found this session breaks capacity or square footage out by individual building.

reading.body:
This facility has no published power specification, no published rack or accelerator count, and no publicly available technical specifications beyond its street address in Centennial, Colorado. The operator, Charter Communications, absorbed Time Warner Cable in 2016 and operates this site as part of its internal infrastructure for cable and internet operations rather than as a marketed data center for external tenants.

Colorado has 17 mapped data center facilities on record, but only 3 publish power consumption figures totaling 26.35 megawatts across the state. This facility ranks fourth by published capacity in Colorado, which means it publishes no capacity figure at all and sits outside the state's small published total.

Without specifications for power draw, cooling, or electrical infrastructure, this campus cannot be assessed against the constraint of grid availability or the scaling capacity it might support for AI workloads. It does not appear in the operator's marketing materials or public product descriptions, and no independent technical audit of its capabilities has been published.
